source.title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex

accepted.question_text: Can the smooth chiral de Rham complex of a compact special-holonomy manifold beyond the Calabi-Yau/K3 setting be used to produce a finite-energy vertex operator algebra and a canonical modular or mock-modular invariant by the following general program: construct two commuting superconformal structures on the smooth chiral de Rham complex, take global sections and BRST cohomology of a left-moving sector to obtain finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces, and decompose that cohomology or its graded dimension into irreducible modules or characters for the right-moving supersymmetry algebra?

evidence.quote: Since the elliptic genus of a Calabi-Yau manifold is the graded dimension of the cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex, it is natural to ask if one can apply the same procedure to other special holonomy manifolds, decomposing ΩchM (resp. its graded dimension) as sums of irreducible modules of the corresponding supersymmetry algebra (resp. its irreducible characters).

We leave several open questions. All of them towards applying the following guideline. 1) construct two commuting superconformal structures on the C∞ chiral de Rham complex. 2) Take global sections (as opposed to sheaf cohomology) and then BRST cohomology of the left moving sector. 3) Decompose this cohomology with respect to the right moving superconformal structure.

What can we do on other special holonomy cases? Can we obtain a vertex operator algebra with finite dimensional energy spaces? can we attach a modular form/function to such a manifold by taking traces of these vertex algebras?

accepted.question_text: What is the geometric meaning of the construction that sends a smooth differential k-form on a Riemannian manifold, together with the Levi-Civita connection, to two global sections J+ and J− of the chiral de Rham complex using local expressions built from the inverse metric, Christoffel symbols, Bessel-polynomial coefficients, ∂γ terms, and the local generators e_i^±? Equivalently, can the corrected normally ordered formula that glues local expressions into global chiral-de Rham sections be characterized by a more intrinsic geometric construction?
accepted.context_brief: Intrinsic meaning of the corrected form-to-section map

evidence.quote: Let now ω ∈ C∞(M, ∧kT∗M) be a smooth k-form. Locally on the coordinate patch U this form is written as Σ wi1,...,ik dxi1 ∧ · · · ∧ dxik.
Theorem 3.14 provides with two embeddings ∧∗ T∗M ֒→ ΩchM, ω 7→ J±.
Each time we increase the degree of the form ω by two we need to insert an extra correcting term of the form Γklgjk∂γl. The geometric meaning of the map (3.14.3) is unclear to the author.

accepted.question_text: Given a Riemannian manifold, let G+ and G− denote the local odd sections of its smooth chiral de Rham complex formed from the bc–βγ fields by adding metric, inverse-metric, Christoffel-symbol, and cubic-fermion correction terms to the flat Boson-Fermion superconformal generators. Is there a topological or geometric invariant whose vanishing characterizes when these local G+ and G− formulas glue to globally defined sections of Ω_ch(M)?
accepted.context_brief: Globality obstruction for curved G± sections

evidence.quote: Note that these G± however are corrections to (3.12.7) involving the Christoffel symbols and a cubic term when the metric is not flat.
4.4 Question. Is there a topological/geometrical invariant for the local sections G± defined by (4.2.1) to be globally defined sections of ΩchM ?
Any remaining term should give a topological/geometrical class on M that should vanish for G± to be well defined.

accepted.question_text: Whenever the local sections G+ and G− given by the curved formula with metric and Christoffel-symbol correction terms glue to global sections of the smooth chiral de Rham complex Ω_ch(M), do they generate two commuting copies of the N=1 superconformal algebra with central charge c = (3/2) dim_R M?
accepted.context_brief: N=1 superconformal algebra generated by global G±

evidence.quote: 4.5 Question. In case G± given by (4.2.1) are globally defined sections of ΩchM, do they generate two commuting copies of the N = 1 superconformal algebra of central charge c = 3/2 dimR M?

The second question is now simply a local computation so it is a matter of computing OPEs in a free field theory of two vectors explicitly given and there exists well established software packages to assist.

accepted.question_text: For a G2-holonomy 7-manifold M, can one define a BRST-type differential Q−_0 on the smooth chiral de Rham complex, analogous to the half-twist differential used in the N=2 and N=4 cases, such that both the cohomology sheaf H(Ω_ch(M), Q−_0) and the cohomology of global sections H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) have finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces?
accepted.context_brief: G2 BRST differential with finite energy spaces

evidence.quote: In the G2 case, the vertex algebra of global sections C∞(M, ΩchM ) is too large, it has infinite dimensional conformal weight spaces.

We would want to perform a half-twist as we did in the previous cases of N = 2 and N = 4 and obtain a vertex algebra with finite dimensional conformal spaces and possibly consider its character as an invariant of M, study its convergence and modular properties, etc.

The first problem is how to define a differential analogous to Q−0 such that its cohomology sheaf H (ΩchM , Q−0 ) has finite dimensional conformal weight spaces? Analogously we would want that the cohomology with respect to Q−0 of the vertex algebra C∞(M, ΩchM ) have finite dimensional conformal weight spaces.

accepted.question_text: For a G2-holonomy manifold, after constructing a BRST-type cohomology of the smooth chiral de Rham complex with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces, what is the character of that cohomology, does it provide an analog of the elliptic genus for G2 manifolds, and does the resulting series converge and have modular properties?

evidence.quote: The second problem is to study its character, this would be the analog of the elliptic genus for a G2 manifold.

It follows that if the answer to the question 4.21 is affirmative, we can attach the formal series χM (τ) = q−21/48strH(ΩchM ,Q−0 ) qL+0 , q = e2πiτ, and ask if this series converges and has modular properties.
Note that since we have two commuting Virasoros: T+, X+ we may promote the above function to a two variable trace by computing the joint eigenspaces of T+0 and X+0.

accepted.question_text: For a G2-holonomy manifold, can one choose or construct the BRST-type differential Q−_0 so that one of the two commuting Shatashvili-Vafa G2 superconformal algebras produced by Rodriguez's theorem commutes with Q−_0, survives in cohomology, and makes the resulting cohomology decompose into irreducible SV^G2 representations whose multiplicity-generating series is a mock modular form canonically attached to M?
accepted.context_brief: G2 SV^G2 representation decomposition and mock modularity

evidence.quote: 4.19 Theorem ([16]). The two sections Φ± generate two commuting copies of the superconformal SV G2 algebra of central charge c = 21/2 in ΩchM in the sense of Remark 2.21.

The third problem and perhaps the most important in connection to Moonshine phenomena is to study the representation of SV G2 in this vertex algebra. We would require that one of the two SV G2 algebras produced by Rodriguez's theorem comutes with Q−0 so that it survives in cohomology.
Rather in this case if the answer to Question 4.21 is affirmative we would consider (4.21.2) as a definition. By Rodriguez theorem this algebra will decompose as irreducible representations of SV G2.

Since one would expect the characters of SV G2 to be mock modular, being obtained by Hamiltonian reduction of osp(4|2) at level k = 1/3 and the character (4.21.2) to be modular, we expect to attach the generating series of multiplicity spaces, a mock modular form, to any G2 manifold.

accepted.question_text: Are the copies of the Shatashvili-Vafa G2 superconformal algebra SV^G2 embedded in the smooth chiral de Rham complex of a G2-holonomy manifold by Rodriguez's theorem simple vertex algebras, so that the Virasoro subalgebra generated by X is the unitary c=7/10 minimal model and the proposed G2 topological twist can be applied?

evidence.quote: The above discussion is only possible if the V ir7/10 generated by X is simple, that is, is a member of the minimal series.
4.21 Question. Are the algebras SV G2 ⊂ ΩchM produced by Rodriguez theorem simple vertex algebras?

The question above, in case of the affirmative, would be an analog to Song's claim in the N = 4 case of the K3 surface. It will also provide a unitary V ir7/10 subalgebra generated by X and hence we can apply the program of [14] to perform the topological twist.

accepted.question_text: For an 8-dimensional manifold M with holonomy Spin(7), does the smooth chiral de Rham complex C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)) carry two global sections X+ and X−, associated with the parallel Spin(7) four-form, that generate two commuting copies of the Shatashvili-Vafa Spin(7) superconformal algebra of central charge 12?

evidence.quote: Let us analyze now the case when the manifold M has holonomy Spin7. These are 8 dimensional manifolds endowed with a four form ψ which is parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection.
Conjecture ([21]). The vertex algebra C∞(M, ΩchM ) carries two global sections X± generating two commuting copies of SV Spin7 of central charge c = 12 as in 2.19 in the sense of Remark 2.21.
The first step would be to prove the conjecture above.

accepted.question_text: For a Spin(7)-holonomy manifold M, is its elliptic genus equal to the graded dimension of the BRST/topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) constructed from the conjectural left-moving SV^Spin7 structure, with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces?
accepted.context_brief: Spin(7) elliptic genus as topological-twist graded dimension

evidence.quote: Assuming that we have two commuting copies of SV Spin7 inside of C∞(M, ΩchM ) we want to obtain the elliptic genus of M as some form of graded dimension of this vertex algebra.

Conjecturally one would obtain a vertex algebra such that its graded dimension: trH(ΩchM ,Q−0 ) qL+0 −c/24, coincides with the elliptic genus of M, in particular, it should have finite dimensional conformal weight spaces.
2 Question. Is the elliptic genus of a Spin7 manifold M the graded dimension of the topological twist H(C∞(M, ΩchM ), Q−0 ) described in 4.22?

accepted.question_text: Are the conjectural characters of unitary representations of the Shatashvili-Vafa Spin(7) algebra used in Spin(7) elliptic-genus decompositions obtained by quantum Hamiltonian reduction of characters of osp(3|2) at level k=1/3, using the Kac-Wakimoto machinery for superconformal algebras and mock theta functions?

evidence.quote: osp(3|2) SV Spin7 1/3 Spin(7)

One would expect to confirm the list of characters of [7] in the Spin7 case by studying the representation theory of osp(3|2) at level k = 1/3 and obtain new characters for the G2 case by studying the representation theory of osp(4|2) at level k = 1/3.
3 Question. Are the conjectural characters of [7] obtained by quantum Hamiltonian reduction of characters of osp(3|2) at level k = 1/3 as described in [41]?

accepted.question_text: Is the decomposition of the Spin(7) elliptic genus Ell_M(τ, α) into characters of the Shatashvili-Vafa Spin(7) algebra induced by decomposing the topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) into irreducible representations of the SV^Spin7 algebra supplied by the conjectural Spin(7) chiral-de Rham construction?
accepted.context_brief: Spin(7) elliptic-genus character decomposition from cohomology

evidence.quote: The proposed characters of SV Spin7 are Mock modular forms and therefore the generating function for the multiplicity spaces is a Mock modular form canonically attached to any Spin7 manifold M.
4 Question. Is the decomposition of EllM(τ, α) in characters of SV Spin7 coming from the decomposition of H(C∞(M, ΩchM ), Q−0 ) into irreducible representations of the SV Spin7 from Conjecture 4.22?

accepted.question_text: Are the vertex algebras produced by the conjectural Spin(7) chiral-de Rham construction irreducible, so that the c=1/2 Virasoro subalgebra is a unitary vertex operator algebra and the smooth chiral de Rham complex decomposes as a sum of irreducible modules, allowing the proposed Spin(7) topological twist to work?
accepted.context_brief: Irreducibility needed for the Spin(7) topological twist

evidence.quote: The Virasoro algebra at c = 1/2 has three irreducible unitary representations, the lowest conformal weight being 0, 1/16 and 1/2 respectively.

Of course the above topological twist in the Spin7 case would only work if the vertex algebras produced by the conjecture are irreducible, so that the copy of V ir1/2 is a unitary vertex operator algebra and ΩchM decomposes as a sum of irreducible modules.

accepted.question_text: Can the supersymmetry algebras inside the chiral de Rham complex of special-holonomy manifolds be constructed directly by quantum Hamiltonian reduction: specifically, is there a morphism from the BRST complex C^•(g, f) defining W_k(g, f) to Ω_ch(M), or to a resolution of Ω_ch(M), that induces the N=2, N=4, SV^Spin7, and SV^G2 embeddings described geometrically?
accepted.context_brief: Direct Hamiltonian-reduction construction of CDR supersymmetries

evidence.quote: The connection between the quantum Hamiltonian reduction and the chiral de Rham complex ΩchM remains a mystery to this day.
All of the supersymmetry algebras of the chiral de Rham complex discussed in the previous section are W algebras.

1 Question. Can one construct the supersymmetries of the chiral de Rham complex directly by Hamiltonian reduction, namely, is there a morphism from C•(g, f) to either ΩchM or perhaps a resolution, inducing the embeddings described in the previous section?
